note: Hand-written expectations for src/rules/rewrite.mjs. Each case gives a source file and either the text it must become (`out`) or the reasons it must be refused (`declined`, as code|specifier|line). `changes` is specifier|target when a rewrite happens. Every case is an import statement, which is why the table is JSON: tools/verify.mjs reads .mjs files looking for exactly that shape and would count these as real dependencies. The refusals outnumber the rewrites on purpose -- that ratio is the claim the tool makes about itself.

cases.why: a default chalk import with covered members: the one rewrite everybody wants
the quote style of the file is kept, because a codemod is not a formatter
the local name is kept when it was renamed at the import
a chained style is checked link by link, and every link here is in the table
optional access reaches a member too, so ?. must not hide one
level and enabled are read off chalk in the wild and both exist here
a member the replacement does not have stops the whole statement, with the line
a bad link late in a chain is still a bad link
passed as a value, so no list of member names describes what the call site needs
one value use is enough to refuse, even beside a member access that would pass
chalk's named exports are a class and per-stream instances; this runtime has neither
one function in, one named function out, under the local name already in use
cases.out:
import { strip as stripAnsi } from 'nirdep/runtime/colour';
console.log(stripAnsi(text));

cases.why: and no pointless alias when the local name already matches the export
named semver imports are checked against what the module actually exports
cases.in:
import { satisfies, major } from 'semver';
satisfies(a, b) && major(a);
cases.out:
import { satisfies, major } from 'nirdep/runtime/semver';
satisfies(a, b) && major(a);

cases.why: a named import of something unimplemented is a build break, not a warning
a namespace import, where every member reached has to be in the table
cases.in:
import * as semver from 'semver';
semver.gt(a, b) || semver.lte(c, d);
cases.out:
import * as semver from 'nirdep/runtime/semver';
semver.gt(a, b) || semver.lte(c, d);

cases.why: semver's classes are reached as members too, and they are not implemented
a dynamic import of chalk survives because the default export is still the default
a dynamic import of strip-ansi does not, because the shape moved to a named export
a loader call reads the value differently, so the file is converted first or not at all
a bare import is here for a side effect the replacement does not have
a re-export passes names through without naming them, so there is nothing to check
an advise-only package is reported and never rewritten, however easy it looks
cases.in:
import minimist from 'minimist';
const a = minimist(argv);

cases.why: supports-color asks the same question through a different shape
eval can reach any name, so nothing static about a binding holds and nothing is touched
a package we do not replace is not our business
two statements in one file, both rewritten, offsets still right for the second
a file with no trailing newline keeps not having one
the same name shadowed inside a function is a different binding, and its members are not ours
a specifier inside a string is text, which is the difference between a lexer and a regex
and so is one inside a comment
a deep path into a package is a different entry point with a different surface
